etymologies.etymologyHTML: The adjective is from Old French liberal, from Latin līberālis (“befitting a freeman”), from līber (“free”); it is attested since the 14th century. The noun is first attested in the 1800s.

definitions.definition: (now rare outside set phrases) Pertaining to those arts and sciences the study of which is considered to provide general knowledge, as opposed to vocational/occupational, technical or mechanical training.

definitions.definition: Generous; permitting liberty; willing to give unsparingly.

quote.citation: 1899, J. M. Baltimore, “Pacific Coast Light Service”, in Overland Monthly, volume 33:
quote.text: Indeed, the Government has been very liberal in the expenditure of public money

quote.citation: 2005, John Gardner, Assessment and Learning, →ISBN, page 50:
quote.text: When he shows improvement she is liberal with her praise and then moves on to the next set of skills to be learnt.

quote.citation: 2007, Helena Page Schrader, The English Templar, →ISBN, page 309:
quote.text: Queen Isabella was already being called Santa Isabella by many of her subjects because she was liberal with her alms.

quote.citation: 2010, Simon Guillebaud, More Than Conquerors: A Call to Radical Discipleship, →ISBN, page 142:
quote.text: Was it because the believers were so liberal with their possessions that God was so liberal with his grace?

quote.citation: 2013 June 14, Jonathan Freedland, “Obama's once hip brand is now tainted”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 1, page 18:
quote.text: Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.

For this reason a liberal amount of piping should be used. If a liberal supply of piping is provided at first, the first cost will of course be greater, but the extra expenditure is called for but once.

quote.citation: 2009, R. Furman Kenney, Chesterville: The Village at the End of the Road, →ISBN, page 102:
quote.text: The result was usually that such helpers got a liberal sprinkling of mud over their clothing.

quote.citation: 2011, Marlene Perez, Dead Is Not an Option, →ISBN, page 37:
quote.text: Rose put a steaming cup of mint tea in front of me and spooned a liberal helping of honey into it.

quote.citation: 1598–1599 (first performance), William Shakespeare, “Much Adoe about Nothing”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene i]:
quote.text: Myself, my brother, and this grieved count,Did see her, hear her, at that hour last night,Talk with a ruffian at her chamber-window;Who hath indeed, most like a liberal villain,Confess'd the vile encounters they have hadA thousand times in secret.

definitions.definition: Widely open to new ideas, willing to depart from established opinions or conventions; permissive.
(politics) Open to political or social changes and reforms associated with either classical or modern liberalism.

quote.citation: 2021, Judith Rainhorn, The Colour of Controversy..., p. 10:
quote.text: Endorsing the liberal anti-interventionist credo that the marketplace should act as the "site of verification," the advocates of white lead opposed government intervention for the sake of open economic competition, which they claimed revealed its true value and thus should be the sole determinant: "When the railways were built, the stage coaches disppeared; they died a timely death. If zinc white is truly superior to white lead, it will kill us in the marketplace, but the government should not intervene." These were the words of Expert-Bezançon, in his February 1903 deposition to the parliamentary committee examining the bill for banning lead-based pigments in paint.

definitions.definition: One with liberal views, supporting individual liberty (see Wikipedia's article on Liberalism).
(US politics) Someone with progressive or left-wing views; one with a left-wing ideology.

quote.citation: 1966, Phil Ochs (lyrics and music), “Love Me, I'm a Liberal”‎[1]:
quote.text: And I love Puerto Ricans and NegrosAs long as they don't move next door.So love me, love me, love me, I'm a liberal.

definitions.definition: (politics)  A supporter of any of several liberal parties.
(UK politics) One who favors individual voting rights, human and civil rights, and laissez-faire markets (also called "classical liberal"; compare libertarian).
(Australian politics) A conservative, especially a liberal conservative.
